1. Purpose. This memorandum directs snow removal and ice mitigation actions for Minot Air Force Base during periods of snow accumulation or freeze-thaw conditions.

2. Tasking. a. 5th Civil Engineer Squadron (5 CES) will plan and execute snow removal to maintain safe installation mobility for mission-essential vehicles, pedestrian access, and emergency response. b. 5 CES will prioritize routes as follows: (1) fire and emergency access routes, (2) routes supporting essential mission operations, (3) main gate and inbound/outbound circulation, and (4) remaining internal roadways. c. 5 CES will apply anti-icing and de-icing materials in accordance with established local guidance and will adjust application rates based on pavement condition and weather forecasts.

3. Unit coordination. a. Organization commanders will ensure designated points of contact (POCs) coordinate with 5 CES for blockage reporting, facility access concerns, and time-sensitive mission requirements. b. Units will remove or relocate vehicles, equipment, and stored items from road shoulders and sidewalks as directed by 5 CES to prevent interference with clearing operations.

4. Public safety. a. All personnel will exercise caution when moving on cleared or partially cleared surfaces and will obey posted warning signage. b. Pedestrian access will be cleared to the extent feasible; however, additional caution is required during active operations and in areas with drifting snow.

5. Reporting. a. When conditions require immediate attention, units will notify 5 CES via the established snow/ice reporting channel. b. Following significant events, 5 CES will provide a summary of completed actions and remaining risk areas to affected stakeholders.

The 49th Maintenance Group will observe an ISO maintenance pause from 2026-06-22 through 2026-06-26 to validate maintenance processes, reconcile technical-order and inspection requirements, and identify actions that improve fleet reliability. Commanders will ensure personnel understand the pause procedures and will report significant risks or mission impacts to the 49 MXG/CC promptly.

This memorandum outlines snow removal responsibilities, priorities, and reporting procedures for Minot Air Force Base to ensure safe and continuous operations during winter weather.

1. Responsibilities.

a. 5 CES/CC is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing snow and ice control for airfield and base infrastructure. This includes plowing, deicing, snow hauling, and application of abrasives and deicers as required to maintain safe conditions.

b. 5 BW/CC will provide command-level prioritization of assets and, when requested, additional resources or authorities to support emergency snow removal operations.

c. All unit commanders will:

- Ensure assigned vehicle and pedestrian routes (including parking lots and walkways) are cleared per locally published priorities.

- Maintain accountability for personnel and equipment tasked to support snow operations.

- Report significant impacts to mission assurance or damage resulting from snow/ice control activities immediately to 5 CES/CC.

2. Priorities.

a. Airfield movement areas (runways, taxiways, aprons) and lifesaving access routes to medical and emergency services are the highest priority.

b. Mission-essential facilities, primary roadways, and building access for mission personnel are secondary priorities.

c. All other areas, including non-mission parking and non-essential walkways, will be cleared as resources permit.

3. Coordination and Notification.

a. 5 CES will monitor weather forecasts and initiate pre-storm preparations per the base Snow and Ice Control Plan. When conditions are forecast to meet or exceed locally established thresholds, 5 CES will notify 5 BW/CC, the Installation Command Post, and affected units.

b. The Installation Command Post will serve as the central point for reporting storm impacts, requests for assistance, and coordination with off-base authorities.

c. Units requiring emergency support will submit requests through the Command Post. For immediate life-safety or flight safety hazards, units will call the Command Post directly.

4. Equipment and Materials.

a. 5 CES will maintain a prioritized list of available snow removal equipment, drivers, and stock levels of deicing materials. Units with organic equipment that can assist should coordinate availability with 5 CES.

b. Requests for additional resources (mutual aid, contracted support) will be routed through 5 BW/CC for approval.

5. Reporting and After-Action.

a. 5 CES will provide 5 BW/CC with daily status reports during prolonged events, to include cleared areas, outstanding priorities, equipment status, and material consumption.

b. Following significant snow events, 5 CES will conduct an after-action review to identify lessons learned and recommend improvements to procedures, staffing, or equipment.

6. Point of Contact.

The primary point of contact for snow removal operations is:

5 CES/CC Comm: (701) XXX-XXXX Email: 5ces.commander@us.af.mil

7. Implementation.

This memorandum is effective immediately. Units will review and, as necessary, update their local procedures to align with the priorities and reporting requirements outlined above.

FIRST M. LAST, Maj, USAF\
FOR THE COMMANDER

MAJ COLIN P. HAYES, Commander Commander, 5 Civil Engineer Squadron

Col Ruth A. Klein, Commander.

This memorandum informs all units and affected personnel that an ISO maintenance pause is in effect for the 49th Wing's information systems. The pause is intended to stabilize core services and minimize risk to operational readiness while essential updates and verifications are performed. Units will experience limited capability assessments, and users may encounter temporary downtime during maintenance windows. Department leads will coordinate any scheduled work with the 49 MXG/CC to minimize impact on mission-critical tasks.

Units are directed to review their current operational procedures and ensure that essential data is backed up and safeguarded. IT liaisons will provide status updates and point-of-contact information as maintenance activities proceed. Any degradation in mission capability should be reported through the normal chain of command to the 49 MXG/CC via the command post; after-hours issues should be escalated to the on-call duty officer.

Per direction from 49 MXG leadership, we will implement an immediate, temporary pause to ISO maintenance activities effective upon receipt of this memorandum. All ISO maintenance tasks will be suspended until further notice to allow for a deliberate review of current processes, safety checks, and parts accountability. Unit maintenance supervisors will secure in-progress work, account for assigned parts and tools, and post status to the maintenance tracking system by the end of duty today.

During the pause, 49 MXG will conduct a focused inspection and risk assessment to identify any systemic issues and to develop corrective actions. Supervisors will prepare a written brief of findings and proposed mitigations for 49 WG/CC within 72 hours. Mission-essential maintenance authorized by my office may continue on a case-by-case basis when preapproved in writing by the maintenance group commander.

AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>

  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF

letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>

To: 12 AF/CC; From: 355 FW/CC

Nominee and scope: Capt Luis Mendez’s selection for the Lance P. Sijan Award rests on a sustained record of valor, leadership, and professional excellence that transcends ordinary performance. Over the reporting period, he coordinated a complex air maneuver with precision under contested conditions, leveraging unconventional airspace management and rapid decision cycles to safeguard casualties and sustain operational momentum. His actions, executed under pressure, reduced risk to personnel and equipment while preserving the integrity of the mission, reflecting the highest standards of the fighter community and the Air Force as a whole.

Across multiple critical adjacencies, Capt Mendez demonstrated a capacity for strategic foresight and team mentorship that elevated unit readiness. He fostered a culture of disciplined initiative, institutionalized meticulous after-action reviews, and authored targeting and threat mitigation solutions that hardened defense postures without compromising tempo. His unwavering accountability, technical acumen, and willingness to assume additional duties under challenging conditions directly enhanced the squadron’s ability to execute high-risk sorties with minimal incident while mentoring junior officers and airmen toward operational independence.

Finally, Capt Mendez embodied the ethos of service before self through a relentless commitment to moral courage and professional development. He led by example in dynamic environments, guided peers through complex ethical decision-making, and institutionalized processes that ensured rapid adaptation to evolving threats. His sustained performance under stress and his quiet, effective leadership undergird unit morale, mission resilience, and the advancement of the Air Force’s core values.

```

I submit, for your consideration, the nomination of Capt Luis Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Award in recognition of an unwavering commitment to professionalism, mission excellence, and the enduring care for people that defines exceptional Airmen. Capt Mendez consistently demonstrates maturity beyond his rank, pairing disciplined execution with the empathy necessary to elevate a team under pressure.

Throughout his tenure, Capt Mendez has been a steady force in translating operational needs into measurable training outcomes, while simultaneously strengthening the unit’s cohesion and resiliency. He has led and improved processes that enhanced readiness and accelerated problem resolution, ensuring that critical standards were understood, practiced, and sustained. Just as importantly, his leadership has remained grounded in mentorship—he listens first, coaches deliberately, and advocates for the removal of barriers so others can succeed. In demanding moments, he remains calm, precise, and accountable, setting conditions for safe, effective execution.

Capt Mendez’s performance reflects the Lance P. Sijan standard of balanced excellence—technical credibility, ethical conduct, and genuine concern for the Airmen he serves alongside. His initiative and follow-through have improved both unit capability and individual confidence, and his example has strengthened a culture where disciplined professionalism is expected and excellence is achieved together. The enclosed AF Form 1206, dated 2026 Jan 30, documents the basis for this nomination.

FOR THE COMMANDER,

COL JOANNA P. REED, Col, USAF Commander, 355th Fighter Wing

As one of the wing’s most trusted combat aviators and mission commanders, Capt Mendez consistently demonstrated the judgment, calm, and technical mastery that turn complex sorties into decisive effects. During the nomination period, Capt Mendez distinguished himself by converting adversity into advantage and uncertainty into momentum. He led demanding operations that required rapid adaptation to changing tasking, weather, and aircraft readiness, while protecting safety, preserving combat power, and delivering results that directly advanced the wing’s flying mission. His influence extended well beyond the cockpit: he mentored junior aviators, strengthened crew coordination, and served as a stabilizing force during high-tempo periods when time, equipment, and personnel were all in short supply. Through initiative and quiet persistence, he helped the squadron meet mission requirements that would have otherwise been delayed, degraded, or displaced.

What most sets Capt Mendez apart is not merely the quantity of his accomplishments, but the character with which he achieved them. He consistently acted with selflessness, humility, and a deep sense of responsibility for the mission and the people entrusted to him, reflecting the very qualities embodied by Capt Lance P. Sijan. His record reveals a leader who never sought recognition, yet repeatedly earned the confidence of peers, supervisors, and subordinates through performance that was both operationally decisive and morally grounded. I strongly recommend Capt Mendez for this award and ask for your favorable consideration of his nomination.

Capt Luis Mendez distinguished himself through exceptional leadership, operational judgment, and sustained commitment to mission success while directing his team through demanding requirements with limited time and competing priorities. He translated commander’s intent into disciplined execution, synchronized personnel and resources across organizational boundaries, and maintained an unrelenting focus on safe, effective outcomes. His ability to anticipate friction, resolve problems before they became mission delays, and communicate clearly at every level strengthened unit performance and gave his teammates the confidence to act decisively when conditions were most challenging.

Capt Mendez’s impact extended well beyond the immediate results of his assigned duties. He cultivated a climate of trust and accountability, deliberately developed Airmen for greater responsibility, and used every setback as an opportunity to improve processes rather than assign blame. By combining technical expertise with genuine investment in people, he improved team cohesion, accelerated the adoption of better practices, and helped create a resilient force prepared to meet future demands. His example inspired peers and subordinates alike, demonstrating the selfless service, moral courage, and warrior ethos expected of an Air Force officer.

Capt Mendez represents the character and caliber envisioned by the Lance P. Sijan Award. His accomplishments reflect not a single successful effort, but a consistent pattern of courageous leadership, personal excellence, and measurable service to the mission and the people entrusted to him. The attached nomination documents the breadth of his contributions and provides the basis for recognizing him as the 355th Fighter Wing’s nominee for this distinguished award. I strongly endorse Capt Mendez’s nomination and respectfully request your favorable consideration.

Per the attached AF Form 1206, I respectfully nominate Capt Luis Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Award. During the nomination period Capt Mendez demonstrated extraordinary leadership, tenacity, and moral courage that significantly exceeded the standards expected of an Air Force officer. He led a high-tempo operations detachment through an extended combined-arms deployment, personally redesigning sortie-generation processes and instituting cross-functional maintenance-training protocols that increased mission capable rates by a measured and sustained margin while directly reducing critical safety risk factors.

Capt Mendez's commitment to his airmen and to mission accomplishment manifested in initiatives that transformed unit culture and readiness. He identified latent talent across his flight, coaching junior officers and enlisted technicians through complex troubleshooting techniques and operational planning; these efforts yielded a measurable uptick in crew proficiency across multiple mission sets and enabled the wing to accept and execute emergent taskings with no increase in manning. When confronted with a cascading logistics shortfall that threatened a critical operation, Capt Mendez negotiated expedited sustainment solutions with higher headquarters and commercial partners, preserving mission momentum without compromising regulatory standards or force protection.

Beyond tactical and operational impact, Capt Mendez advanced institutional priorities through professional scholarship and mentorship that multiplied his effect throughout the enterprise. He authored a unit-level procedural revision that harmonized sortie documentation practices across three squadrons, reducing administrative overhead and improving data fidelity for readiness reporting; concurrently he championed an inclusive mentorship program that increased retention intent among junior NCOs and officers. Taken together, these accomplishments reflect the character, leadership, and selfless service the Lance P. Sijan Award recognizes, and I endorse his nomination for consideration by your board.

1. Purpose. This memorandum provides implementation guidance for parental leave policy across Air Force organizations and is intended to promote consistent execution, timely approval, and equitable treatment of eligible members.

2. Eligibility. Parental leave is available to eligible Service members in accordance with governing Department of the Air Force policy and applicable statutory authorities. Commanders and supervisors will ensure requests are evaluated based on the member's qualifying event and leave entitlement, and will not impose local restrictions that conflict with higher-level guidance.

3. Documentation. Members will submit parental leave requests through the established leave approval process and provide any supporting documentation required to verify eligibility and entitlement. Units will maintain records in accordance with applicable records management and leave tracking requirements.

Major command points of contact will coordinate unresolved policy questions with HQ USAF/A1 through established personnel policy channels. Commands will distribute this guidance to subordinate units and supervisors responsible for approving parental leave.

Purpose. This memorandum provides implementation guidance for the parental leave policy recently published by Headquarters, Department of the Air Force. It clarifies eligibility, required documentation, and responsibilities to ensure uniform application across all Air Force major commands (ALMAJCOMs).

Eligibility. Parental leave is available to eligible Service members and civilian employees in accordance with the governing policy. Eligibility criteria include birth or placement of a child through adoption or foster care and applicable service or employment status requirements. Duration, pay, and timeline provisions follow the policy; commands must consult the governing instruction and their servicing personnel offices for case-specific determinations.

Documentation. Requests for parental leave must be submitted through established personnel systems with supporting documentation attached, such as a birth certificate, adoption paperwork, or placement documentation. Medical certification and commander endorsement may be required where specified by policy. Records supporting leave requests must be maintained per applicable records management and privacy guidance.

Points of Contact. For questions regarding eligibility, entitlements, and processing procedures, ALMAJCOMs should contact HQ USAF/A1 Work-Life Policy at usaf.a1.worklife@us.af.mil or (703) 695-0000, and their servicing personnel office for local execution details.

```

Hurricane relief operations require immediate force-generation actions to provide timely airlift, medical evacuation, and communications support. ACC is directing the 23d Wing to prepare and align available forces for rapid employment in support of affected communities and civil authorities.

The 23d Wing will generate and make available the forces necessary to support hurricane relief operations, consistent with applicable readiness, safety, and coordination requirements. Complete all actions below no later than the suspense stated in the subject.

- Airlift

  - Identify available aircraft, aircrews, and support personnel capable of transporting personnel, relief supplies, and equipment.

  - Report force availability, mission limitations, and earliest deployment timelines to ACC/A3.

- Medical Evacuation

  - Identify aeromedical evacuation aircraft, crews, medical teams, and required support equipment.

  - Confirm patient movement capacity, receiving-facility coordination, and readiness to deploy.

- Communications

  - Identify deployable communications packages, operators, and maintenance support.

  - Confirm interoperability, redundant communications capability, and earliest availability for employment.

- Medevac (MEDEVAC)

  - Ensure medically equipped aircraft and trained crews are positioned to evacuate critically injured/ill from incident areas to definitive care.

  - Coordinate with local hospitals and regional medical C2 for patient tracking, inbound flow, and clinical handover.

- Comms

  - Deploy or re-task comms assets to restore commander/situation awareness and interagency coordination; ensure redundant voice/data paths for command and control across affected zones.

No classification. No indorsement.

  - "355 FW/CC"
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

subject: "Nomination of Capt Luis Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Award."
date: "2026-01-31"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.

tag_line: ""

dissemination: ""

references: []

cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.

The selection of Capt Mendez for the Lance P. Sijan Leadership Award acknowledges his enduring impact, exemplary integrity, and selfless service. It is with confidence and pride that this nomination is forwarded for esteemed consideration."}

This memorandum documents the 4th Fighter Wing's recent bird aircraft strike hazard activity and identifies corrective actions to reduce the risk of additional strikes. Safety personnel reviewed the reported events, associated airfield conditions, and operational patterns.

The reviewed strike events occurred at the following times and locations:

> 2026-05-06, 0815L — Runway 16 approach end\
> 2026-05-07, 1420L — Taxiway Bravo near the perimeter road\
> 2026-05-08, 1745L — Runway 34 departure end

The pattern indicates recurring bird activity near aircraft movement areas during periods of increased flight operations. All units should continue prompt reporting of strikes, near misses, and significant bird concentrations through established channels.

I recommend the following mitigations:

- Increase active bird dispersal coverage during identified high-activity periods.

  - Position qualified personnel near the runway approach and departure ends before the first scheduled sortie.

  - Record dispersal actions and observed flock movement in the daily airfield wildlife log.

- Reduce attractants and improve habitat management around the airfield.

  - Coordinate removal of standing water, food sources, and other conditions that attract birds.

  - Inspect the perimeter and movement areas weekly and track corrective actions to closure.

The 4 FW/SE will monitor implementation and provide a follow-up assessment after 30 days. Questions or additional observations should be directed to the 4 FW Safety Office.

1. Situation. A Category 4 hurricane made landfall within ACC's area of responsibility, causing widespread infrastructure damage, population displacement, and degraded civil response capabilities. Local authorities have declared a state of emergency and requested DoD support. Rapid deployment of airlift, medical evacuation, and resilient communications assets is required to support life-saving and life-sustaining operations.

2. Mission. ACC/A3 directs 23 WG/CC to immediately generate and prepare aircrew, aircraft, and support personnel for hurricane relief operations to commence in support of civil authorities no later than 4 Sep 2026.

3. Specified tasks:

- Airlift:

  - Task (a). Generate a minimum of two C-17 or C-130 sorties per day to move disaster relief personnel, water, food, and critical equipment into designated support hubs until local supply chains are re-established.

  - Task (b). Prepare to execute intra-theater airlift and aeromedical evacuation routing as directed by the Joint Task Force.

- Medevac:

  - Task (a). Posture aeromedical evacuation crews and equipment to conduct patient movement from impacted areas to higher-echelon medical facilities; ensure MEDEVAC configuration and medical staffing meet clinical requirements.

  - Task (b). Coordinate with local medical authorities and DoD medical elements for patient prioritization and transmission logistics.

- Comms:

  - Task (a). Deploy expeditionary communications packages to provide command, control, and emergency telecommunications at reception hubs and forward operating locations.

  - Task (b). Establish redundant voice and data links to support operations, including SATCOM and line-of-sight networks as required.

FOR THE COMMANDER

COLTON B. GRAVES, Maj Gen, USAF Director of Operations

This memorandum documents a Bird Aircraft Strike Hazard (BASH) after action and provides recommendations to mitigate near-term recurrence.

On 2026-05-08 three bird strikes occurred during flight operations. Details follow.

> 0715 Z — Approach, Runway 27\
> Aircraft contacted a flock on final approach; minor airframe damage, no injuries.\\
>
> 1030 Z — Departure, Runway 09\
> Bird ingestion during initial climb; engine inspection required, flight delayed.\\
>
> 1435 Z — Taxiway B near Taxiway C intersection\
> Strike to left wing leading edge during taxi; superficial damage only.

2. The tasking requires the deployment of a ready force to support hurricane relief efforts within the specified timeframe.

- A. Airlift: Mobilize aircraft and aircrew for swift transportation of relief personnel and supplies.

- B. Medevac: Prepare medical evacuation teams and facilities for rapid response.

- C. Communications: Establish reliable communication links to coordinate response efforts effectively.

> Maj Gen COLTON B. GRAVES, Director of Operations\
> Department of the Air Force

The legal basis for the order is supported by the following authorities:

- (a) AFI 31-115, *Law Enforcement Operations*, which governs the establishment and enforcement of off-limits areas to ensure the safety and security of Air Force personnel and resources.

- (c) Jurisprudence affirming the commander's authority to regulate conduct on military installations to maintain good order and discipline.

This review endorses the proposed Off-Limits Order as compliant with applicable law and policy, provided it is implemented with clear communication to all affected parties and consistent enforcement.

On its face the proposed restrictions are within the commander’s authority to protect the health, safety, and welfare of the force, provided the factual basis supporting each listed location is documented and reasonably related to the stated purpose.

Legal support for issuing an off-limits order in this instance includes the following bases:

- The commander’s inherent authority to take measures necessary to preserve good order and discipline and protect mission readiness.

  - This authority permits reasonable, narrowly tailored restrictions when supported by articulable facts showing a genuine threat to the force.

- Regulatory authorization under AFI 31-115, *Law Enforcement Operations*.

  - AFI 31-115 discusses force protection and collaboration with installation commanders and Security Forces in establishing conditions that may warrant access restrictions.

- Civilian law and constitutional considerations permitting restrictions on access when they are content-neutral, time/place/manner regulations that are reasonably tailored to serve a significant government interest and leave open ample alternative channels for lawful conduct.

  - Ensure any order is drafted to avoid vague or overbroad language that could unnecessarily restrict protected activity or exceed the commander’s authority.

If you concur, the legal office can prepare a finalized order that incorporates the recommended factual findings, clarifies the temporal and spatial scope of each restriction, and includes notice and appeal information for affected personnel.

To: 25 AF/A2 From: 9 IS/CC

Subject: CTI Handling for Partner Air Forces

This memorandum provides guidance on the handling, dissemination, and safeguarding of Counter-Intelligence information (CTI) related to partner Air Forces. All CTI material associated with partner nations should be treated with heightened sensitivity and restricted to personnel with an operational need-to-know. Operators and intelligence personnel must ensure that CTI is accessed only by cleared individuals and that dissemination to partner forces complies with applicable DoD and Air Force policies, including NOFORN restrictions when applicable. A formal, risk-based approach should be used to determine which elements of CTI can be shared and under what circumstances, with proper documentation and oversight.

This guidance emphasizes the importance of maintaining situational awareness of partner capabilities, vulnerabilities, and intent, while preventing unintended exposure of sensitive CTI sources and methods. Partners should be engaged through authorized channels, and all exchanges should be logged and audited to maintain accountability and compliance with security requirements.

Two paragraphs:

The Air Force Training Wing requests approval to increase the number of SIM sorties available to IFF (Identification Friend or Foe) students due to scheduling constraints and the need to reinforce practical decision-making under realistic stress. This initiative will focus on core IFF procedures, threat recognition, and communication discipline during simulated air-to-air and air-to-ground scenarios. The objective is to reinforce critical IFF skills, ensure consistent proficiency across the cohort, and reduce bottlenecks in the live-fly training pipeline.

The four additional simulations are designed to fit within existing flying hour constraints while expanding exposure to diverse engagement contexts. Each event will be conducted under standard safety and debrief protocols, with instructors assessing student performance and providing targeted feedback.

- Further SIM event A: Integrated IFF and radio communication drill in mixed-traffic airspace, with emphasis on secure IFF replies and threat evaluation.

- Further SIM event B: Multi-ship scenario focusing on cooperative identification and collision avoidance within a constrained corridor.

- Further SIM event C: Pre-flight checklist and post-flight debrief focusing on IFF data integrity and report accuracy under time pressure.

- Further SIM event D: Controlled adversary IFF challenge with randomized cues to test rapid decision-making and IFF integrity verification.

To increase repetition and build confidence before IFF students enter live training, the 33d Operations Group will provide four additional simulator events. Squadron schedulers will coordinate student availability, instructor coverage, and simulator time to place these events before the applicable evaluation or sortie.

The additional events will focus on mission-relevant decision-making and disciplined execution. Each event will be tailored to the student's training progression and documented in the appropriate training records.

  - **Event 3:** Beyond-visual-range intercept setup, emphasizing timeline management, sensor employment, and weapons employment decisions.

  - **Event 4:** Integrated mission scenario, emphasizing threat reactions, formation coordination, and recovery procedures.

The 33d Operations Group requests approval for the addition of four simulation (SIM) sorties to the training curriculum for Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) students. These additional sorties will enhance student proficiency and readiness by providing greater exposure to simulated operational conditions. This memorandum outlines the proposed extra SIM events to be incorporated into the training schedule.

The following four additional SIM events are proposed for scheduling:

- a. SIM Event Alpha: Focus on rapid identification protocols under simulated combat stress conditions.
- b. SIM Event Bravo: Emphasis on joint-force coordination exercises using multi-platform identification systems.
- c. SIM Event Charlie: Simulation of electronic warfare interference scenarios to train adaptive recognition responses.
- d. SIM Event Delta: Advanced threat recognition drills incorporating simulated hostile electronic countermeasures.

These additional sorties aim to strengthen student capabilities and mission preparedness prior to live-flight training phases.

  These additional sorties aim to strengthen student capabilities and mission preparedness prior to live-flight training phases.
~~~

The KC-135 Formal Training Unit (FTU) continues to meet mission requirements with respect to student throughput, sortie generation, and graduation rates. Current manning and pipeline timing have improved overall training efficiency, reducing average time to qualification by approximately two weeks since the last assessment. Cumulative student throughput remains on track to meet the annual objectives as occupancy of FTU training slots remains at or near established thresholds, with watch-bill optimization and enhanced scheduling coordination contributing to this performance.

To sustain this trajectory, we will continue to monitor pipeline bottlenecks, maintain targeted instructor-to-student ratios, and execute periodic curriculum updates aligned with field feedback and tanker readiness demands. 1. The 18 WG/CC convened a commander's conference offsite on 2026-04-28 to review wing priorities, assess execution risk, and record decisions for follow-up action. Attendance is recorded below.

> COL JAMES A. HART, 18 WG/CC\
> CMSGT LISA M. TURNER, 18 WG/CCC\
> LTCOL MICHAEL R. KANE, 18 WG/JA\
> MAJ SARAH P. NGUYEN, 18 WG/XP\
> CAPT ERIC D. MILLER, 18 WG/HC\
> MSgt DANIEL T. REYES, 18 WG/COM\
> TSgt AMANDA L. BROWN, 18 WG/PA\
> 1ST LT OLIVIA N. PARK, 18 WG/SE

2. Decision: The wing will prioritize mission readiness actions that close the most significant gaps before the next quarter.

   - a. Each group commander will identify the top three readiness barriers affecting their unit.

   - b. Wing staff will consolidate inputs and provide a single tracker to the commander NLT 2026-05-05.

   - c. The vice group commanders will monitor execution and elevate issues that require command intervention.

3. Decision: The wing will standardize offsite reporting and battle rhythm products to reduce duplication and improve speed of decision.

   - a. Staff offices will use a common slide format for recurring updates beginning with the next staff meeting.

   - b. The plans office will publish a one-page decision log template for all future commander conferences.

   - c. Action owners will annotate suspense dates, dependencies, and risk statements on every deliverable.

4. Decision: The wing will sustain morale and communication improvements identified during the offsite.

   - a. Supervisors will reinforce a leader presence model at squadron level and increase visible engagement with Airmen.

   - b. Public affairs will prepare a short internal recap highlighting the three decisions above and the associated next steps.

   - c. The command chief will track feedback from the field and advise the commander on follow-on communication actions.

This memorandum for record documents the decisions reached during the 18 WG/CC commander's conference conducted as part of the wing offsite on April 28, 2026. Twelve personnel participated in the offsite. The following eight attendees are recorded by name and grade:

> LEON W. PRUITT, Brig Gen, USAF\
> MARCUS T. REED, Col, USAF\
> AMY R. SANTIAGO, Col, USAF\
> JONATHAN K. PRICE, Lt Col, USAF\
> NATALIE E. FIELDS, Lt Col, USAF\
> DAVID L. MORAN, Maj, USAF\
> KELLY J. WATKINS, Maj, USAF\
> ROBERT H. CHEN, CMSgt, USAF

The conference established the following readiness priorities for the next planning cycle:

- Align squadron readiness reporting to the wing battle rhythm.

  - Commanders will review reporting criteria at their next staff meeting.

  - The wing staff will publish a consolidated reporting calendar by May 15, 2026.

- Focus exercise preparation on deployable mission-essential tasks.

  - Each group will identify its two highest-risk tasks.

  - The inspector general will incorporate those risks into the next assessment plan.

The conference approved a unified approach to installation and mission support:

- Prioritize resources that directly improve sortie generation and operational availability.

  - Resource proposals will identify the mission effect, expected benefit, and execution risk.

  - The comptroller will provide a decision-quality summary for the next corporate board.

- Improve cross-functional coordination before major execution events.

  - Group commanders will designate a primary and alternate coordination representative.

  - The staff will use a single decision log for unresolved support issues.

1. PURPOSE: This Memorandum for Record captures decisions approved during the 18 WG/CC Commander’s Conference at a 12-person offsite held on 2026-04-28.

> LEON W. PRUITT, Brig Gen, USAF\
> CAMILLE R. HENDERSON, Col, USAF\
> JAMES T. RAMIREZ, Lt Col, USAF\
> ANGELA M. KIM, Lt Col, USAF\
> KEVIN D. LARSON, Maj, USAF\
> SARA N. PATEL, Maj, USAF\
> ROBERT J. HARRIS, Capt, USAF\
> NATALIE O. REED, Capt, USAF

2. DECISION: Prioritize Mission Readiness Sprint (MRS) deliverables for the next 90 days.

- Confirmed top MRS focus areas:

  - Airfield capability and surge readiness

  - Weapons and munition accountability validation

  - Training throughput and qualification recency

- Directed the following actions:

  - Publish a consolidated MRS scorecard by 2026-05-05

  - Conduct a weekly executive review every Thursday

- Established governance:

  - Use color-coded risk reporting for schedule and resourcing

  - Require written mitigation plans for any “red” item within 72 hours

3. DECISION: Standardize the wing’s internal process for rapid incident response and after-action learning.

- Approved the incident response sequence:

  - Immediate stabilization actions under the applicable functional lead

  - Fact-finding within the first business day

  - Corrective action identification before the 5th workday

- Required documentation expectations:

  - Common template for incident briefs and AARs

  - Single repository with version control for all final outputs

- Reinforced a learning loop:

  - Share “what changed and why” during the next commander-led forum

  - Track corrective action closure to completion with named owners

4. DECISION: Align manpower, space, and funding assumptions to enable sustained training and modernization.

- Determined near-term resourcing principles:

  - Protect critical training days and recurring readiness checks

  - Route modernization requests through a single prioritized intake

  - Balance cross-functional support to prevent execution gaps

- Directed planning milestones:

  - Provide draft resourcing assumptions by 2026-05-12

  - Present the finalized assumptions at the next wing leadership standup

- Noted success measures:

  - Reduced variance between forecasted and executed training outputs

  - Improved timelines for corrective actions and recurring task completion

```

LEON W. PRUITT, Brig Gen, USAF, Commander
```

This Memorandum for Record captures the decisions and action guidance from an 18 WG/CC commander's conference held offsite on 2026-04-28. The wing commander recorded decisions reached by the 12-person conference; the items below summarize the agreed actions, owners, and timelines.

> COLIN A. HAWKINS, Col, USAF\
> MARIA L. SANTIAGO, Lt Col, USAF\
> TYRONE J. BARKER, Maj, USAF\
> ERICA V. NGUYEN, Capt, USAF\
> RYAN T. O'NEIL, SMSgt, USAF\
> KAREN P. LOPEZ, GS-13\
> DERRICK S. HOLLOWAY, Civ, DoD\
> ANNA M. FELTON, Capt, USAF

Decision 1: Consolidate maintenance scheduling to reduce sortie delay.

- Action: Implement a single integrated maintenance schedule across flying and back-shop units.

  - Owner: Maintenance Operations (MO)

  - Timeline: Initial integrated schedule published (30 days); full transition (120 days).

- Expected outcome: Reduce sortie delays by 15% within 6 months and improve parts accountability.

Decision 2: Improve security and access control for transient aircraft operations.

- Action: Revise transient aircraft SOPs and add one dedicated security liaison at the transient ramp.

  - Owner: Wing Security Forces / Air Mobility Liaison

  - Timeline: Revised SOPs issued (45 days); liaison assigned immediately.

- Resources: Budget request for liaison funding and access-control kiosk submitted to Comptroller for next quarter.

Decision 3: Enhance leader development and cross-functional training opportunities.

- Action: Establish a quarterly leader-development seminar and a rotating cross-functional shadow program.

  - Owner: 18 WG/CC (oversight) and Force Development cell (execution)

  - Timeline: Seminar calendar published (60 days); shadow program pilot (90 days).

- Metrics: Track participation rates, post-program leader self-assessments, and mission-effectiveness indicators; brief results to the commander at the quarterly commander's update.

LEON W. PRUITT Brig Gen, USAF Commander

The 366th Fighter Wing Safety Office conducted operational risk management spot checks across selected wing activities. The checks assessed whether personnel were applying ORM processes during planning and execution, documenting identified hazards, and implementing appropriate controls. Overall, personnel demonstrated a sound understanding of ORM requirements, and most observed activities reflected effective risk-based decision-making.

Several opportunities for improvement were identified, primarily involving incomplete documentation of control measures and inconsistent communication of residual risk. Supervisors should reinforce these practices during recurring training and pre-task briefings, and offices should review their local procedures to ensure ORM documentation remains current and readily available. The Safety Office will continue follow-up checks to measure progress and provide assistance as needed.

Reviews should address training, planning, execution, communications, and integration with supported ground forces and other air and space capabilities.

AF/A3 will consolidate submissions and develop a proposed doctrine update for senior-leader review. Submit findings and recommendations by established headquarters suspense through command channels; questions may be directed to AF/A3 doctrine staff.

3. AF/A3 will provide a draft revision and recommended implementation plan no later than 2027-03-31. Direct any questions through my action officer, and ensure all coordinating inputs identify unresolved issues, proposed changes, and any impacts to training, readiness, or force presentation.

memo_for:
  - 55 WG/CC
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.

memo_from:
  - 55 OG/CC
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Open Source Media Training
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-10-03 # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.

letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>

letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""

tag_line: ""

references: []

cc: []

distribution: []

attachments: []

memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

This memorandum provides notice of an Open Source Media Training to familiarize unit public affairs and operations personnel with best practices for identifying, assessing, and responsibly engaging with open source information. The training will cover methods for verifying online sources, assessing credibility, basic legal and policy considerations for public releases, and guidance on coordinating with higher headquarters and public affairs channels to ensure accurate and authorized dissemination.

Attendance is requested for all personnel assigned to public affairs, information operations, and mission planning sections to ensure consistent application of standards across the wing. Please coordinate scheduling and attendee lists through 55 OG/PA. Point of contact for this training is Capt Jane D. Example at jane.example@us.af.mil or (555) 123-4567.

This memorandum directs an immediate review and refresh of Close Air Support (CAS) doctrine to ensure alignment with evolving multi-domain operational concepts, advances in munitions and sensor capabilities, and joint force interoperability requirements.

The Director of Operations (AF/A3) will coordinate with Major Command (MAJCOM) operations directors, Air Combat Command, Air Force Special Operations Command, and appropriate joint and coalition partners to draft updated doctrine. The review will prioritize procedures that improve target identification, reduce fratricide risk, integrate joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) employment across contested environments, and refine command-and-control relationships for distributed operations.

MAJCOMs will designate a single point of contact to participate in the doctrine working group, provide current CAS tactics, techniques, and procedures, and submit recommended changes no later than 60 days from the date of this memorandum. The AF/A3 staff will consolidate inputs, produce a draft doctrine update for coordination, and publish final guidance in accordance with statutory and Department of the Air Force policy timelines.

Parking for the Christmas Extravaganza will be limited due to increased visitor attendance and event staging. Personnel are encouraged to carpool, use available shuttle services from designated remote lots, or seek alternate transportation where feasible.

1. Effective immediately, direct a 48-hour safety down day for all assigned and attached 388 FW units beginning 0001L, 15 June 2026, and ending 2359L, 16 June 2026.

2. During this period, suspend non-mission-essential flying, ground maintenance, continuation training, ancillary training, and discretionary equipment operations. Mission-essential sorties, alerts, and activities required to preserve force protection, nuclear surety, weapons security, or emergency response capability may continue only with my explicit approval or that of the OG/CC for immediate operational necessity.

3. Use the down day to conduct deliberate safety stand-down events, review procedures and risk controls, reinforce supervision expectations, and address the causal and contributing factors associated with the recent Class C mishap. I expect frank discussion, unit-level risk assessments, and documented corrective actions where applicable.

4. Coordinate any required deviations through the chain of command. Ensure this direction is disseminated to all squadron commanders, flight commanders, and senior enlisted leaders no later than 1200L, 14 June 2026.

5. Provide me a consolidated status update NLT 1700L, 16 June 2026, summarizing completion of stand-down actions, any mission impacts, and recommended follow-on measures.

RYAN T. HAWKINS, Col, USAF Commander

```

  - Commander, 48th Fighter Wing

1. Effective 2026-09-04 at 0001L through 2026-09-05 at 2359L, all 48th Fighter Wing personnel will execute a 48-hour safety stand-down in response to a Class C mishap.

2. During this period, operations and maintenance activities will pause except for essential actions required to preserve safety, prevent damage, and support mission-critical tasks approved by the Operations Group Commander and Wing Safety.

3. The Operations Group will:

- Conduct immediate safety briefings for all aircrew, maintainers, and support personnel to review the mishap summary, human factors considerations, and interim controls.

- Implement a unit-level risk assessment for all remaining sorties/tasks scheduled immediately after stand-down, ensuring required configuration, weapon system, and equipment checks are performed prior to returning to flight.

- Ensure all aircraft and associated support equipment are inspected for applicable findings and deferred deficiencies are documented in the appropriate records.

4. The focus for the stand-down will be learning, disciplined risk management, and verification of controls—not resuming routine operations by default.

5. Provide the Wing Commander a consolidated summary no later than 2026-09-06 1200L. The summary will include stand-down attendance, completed briefings, interim corrective actions initiated, and any issues requiring Wing-level decision or additional resources.

6. Compliance with this directive is mandatory. If an exception is required, coordinate through the Operations Group Commander and Wing Safety for approval prior to execution.

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0 # keep verbatim
$kind: main
memo_for:
  - 19 AW/CC
memo_from:
  - 19 AW/A3
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Christmas Extravaganza Parking # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-12-15 # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: FOR THE COMMANDER # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - MAJ OLIVIA C. NASH, USAF
  - Director of Operations
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dod # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: UNCLASSIFIED
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

Effective immediately, direct a 48-hour safety down day for all 23d Operations Group flying and sortie-generation activities in response to the Class C mishap that occurred on April 16, 2026. The safety down day will begin at 0001 hours local time on April 18, 2026, and conclude at 2359 hours local time on April 19, 2026. This direction applies to all assigned and attached fighter squadrons and to associated maintenance, intelligence, aircrew flight equipment, and operations-support personnel.

During the safety down day, suspend all training, operational, and test sorties except those specifically approved by me for urgent national-defense requirements, aircraft recovery, or mishap-response support. Preserve mishap evidence and records, and ensure no maintenance action disturbs relevant components or documentation unless required to protect personnel or property.

Use this period to complete a focused review of flight and ground-safety practices, aircraft and equipment status, current risk assessments, crew-rest compliance, and supervisory controls. Conduct face-to-face all-hands safety briefings before resuming normal operations. Squadron commanders will document identified hazards, immediate corrective actions, and unresolved risks, and provide those results to the Operations Group commander no later than 1200 hours local time on April 20, 2026.

Before authorizing the first sortie after the down day, provide me a consolidated assessment through the 23d Wing Safety Office confirming completion of the reviews and briefings, disposition of all immediately correctable hazards, and acceptance or mitigation of any remaining risk. No commander will treat schedule recovery or mission demand as grounds to bypass this direction.

Coordinate implementation with the 23d Wing Safety Office and the 366th Fighter Wing Inspector General as appropriate. Direct questions or requests for exception through your chain of command to the 23d Wing Commander.

Effective immediately, all flying and ground operations within the 355th Fighter Wing are directed to cease for a 48-hour Safety Down Day. This action is in response to the Class C mishap that occurred on 11 May 2026.

The purpose of the Safety Down Day is to conduct comprehensive safety briefings, vehicle and equipment inspections, and hazard identification exercises. Commanders at all levels are tasked to ensure all personnel strictly adhere to the suspension of normal operations and fully engage in safety activities.

All unit commanders will report the status of their Safety Down Day inspections and actions to the Operations Group Commander's office by 14 May 2026 at 1600 hours.

This directive aims to reinforce a culture of safety, prevent further mishaps, and ensure the continued readiness and welfare of personnel and equipment.

POINT OF CONTACT for this directive is Maj Sarah T. Collins, 355 FW/SE, extension 555-1234.

Thank you for your immediate attention and cooperation.

JAMES R. CARTER BRIGADIER GENERAL, USAF COMMANDER, 355TH FIGHTER WING

{"content":"~~~
$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - ORG1/SYMBOL
  - ORG2/SYMBOL
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: !must_fill # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

The first paragraph. Top-level paragraphs are auto-numbered; do not add manual numbering.

- Nested bullets are automatically lettered.

Lines that take no number, letter, or bullet — a roster of names, an address — go in a block quote, typeset as written. End a line with a backslash to break it.

> FIRST M. LAST, Maj, USAF\
> SECOND N. LAST, Capt, USAF

~~~
$kind: indorsement
# composable (0..N)
# An endorsing official's response to the memo, or their forwarding of it onward. Indorsements are numbered in card order: 1st Ind, 2d Ind, 3d Ind.
# Office symbol or Rank Name of the endorsing official.
from: !must_fill ORG/SYMBOL # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Office symbol or organization receiving the endorsed memo.
for: !must_fill ORG/SYMBOL # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# YYYY-MM-DD, the date the endorser signs or forwards the memo — distinct from the originating memo's date, per AFH 33-337 Ch. 14. Leave blank to print a fillable PDF text field for the endorser to type into when signing.
date: "" # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Authority line for this indorsement, printed in uppercase above its signature block. An indorsement has a closing section of its own, so the same rules apply: fill it in when the endorser signs for the commander or the headquarters, leave it blank when the commander signs.
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# 'standard' keeps the indorsement on the action document's page under a one-line header, and moves it to a page of its own, under the fuller header, when it no longer fits. 'separate_page' always begins a new page. 'informal' prints no header at all, so an informal indorsement with an empty body is nothing but a signature block — with no text of its own to hold it to the page, it can open a page alone. Give it a body or an action, or use 'standard'.
format: standard # enum<standard | informal | separate_page>
# The endorser's decision, printed as an either/or line with the choice underlined and the rejected option struck out. Leave blank to omit the line. The wording follows the indorsement's place in the chain: the last one is the approval authority and reads Approve/Disapprove, every earlier one is a coordinating official and reads Concur/Nonconcur. Use 'undecided' to print the pair unmarked, for the endorser to mark by hand.
action: "" # enum<undecided | approve | disapprove>
~~~

Write indorsement body here.
"}

The undersigned authorizes the 88th Communications Squadron, Wright-Patterson AFB, to issue temporary SIPR (Secret) network access tokens to forty (40) deploying maintainers assigned to support mission-essential communications and repair work associated with current operations. The tokens are to be issued for a temporary window while these personnel are deployed or otherwise away from their home station.

Suspense: 2026-09-15. All tokens must be issued, secured, and tracked in accordance with applicable DoD and USAF policy and the squadrons SIPR token management procedure. Tokens will be limited to the minimum required scope of access for the deployers duty tasks and must be deactivated and returned to the unit when deployment or assignment ends or upon request of the Information Assurance or Security Office. There shall be a contemporaneous audit trail for issuance, modification, and revocation.

Issuance responsibilities:

- Security and management: The Squadron Information Assurance Officer (IAO) or designated authority shall authorize token creation, assign the scope, expiry, and revocation conditions, and ensure appropriate monitoring.

- Token characteristics: Each token is restricted to the user and to the specified mission needs; tokens will be time-bound and automatically expire on the final day of the deployment window unless extended in writing by the approving authority.

- Accountability and reporting: All token issuance actions and revocations shall be recorded in the unit's SIPR token management system with a functional justification. A daily roll-up report shall be forwarded to the Squadron Commander and the Wing Information Security Office.

Distribution: This action memo is to be circulated to the 88th Communications Squadron Tenant Units as required for operational awareness and compliance.

This memorandum directs immediate safety actions following a Class C mishap involving a wing aircraft on 12 May 2026. The wing commander has determined a focused 48-hour safety down day is required to ensure all safety, maintenance, and operational risk management measures are complete before resuming normal flight operations.

1. Effective 0000 local, 15 May 2026, the 4th Fighter Wing (4FW) imposes a 48-hour safety down day for all flight and flying-related operations. The safety down day will end at 2359 local, 16 May 2026, unless extended in writing by the Wing Commander.

2. During the safety down day, the following actions are mandatory:

   a. All flight operations, sorties, and sortie generation directly supporting flight training, local aircrew proficiency, and operational missions are suspended. Non-flying mission-essential tasks (e.g., intelligence, command and control) that do not require aircraft will continue unless otherwise directed.

   b. Commanders at all levels will ensure each aircrew and maintenance member completes a mandatory safety brief led by their unit safety representative covering:

   - Details and initial findings related to the Class C mishap (as releasable),

   - Human factors and risk-environment considerations, and

   - Flight and maintenance standardization reminders and error mitigation techniques.

   c. Maintenance organizations will conduct focused inspections on aircraft and associated ground support equipment, to include:

   - A documented walk-around and systems check of affected aircraft types,

   - Verification of recent maintenance actions and configuration control, and

   - Spot inspections of maintenance logs for procedural compliance.

   d. Unit commanders will review local procedures, crew-rest and scheduling practices, and aircrew training currency to identify potential systemic contributors to the mishap.

   e. All personnel will report safety-related observations or potential hazards through established channels (e.g., ASAP, Military Flight Operations Quality Assurance reporting where applicable, or direct report to unit safety). Significant findings shall be elevated to Wing Safety immediately.

3. The Wing Safety Office (4FW/SE) will:

   a. Lead the wing-level mishap response and coordinate initial fact-finding consistent with AFI 91-204 and applicable investigation guidance.

   b. Provide consolidated safety brief material and inspection checklists to units by 0800 local, 15 May 2026.

   c. Maintain a daily summary of findings and corrective actions and provide a report to the Wing Commander not later than 1700 local, 16 May 2026.

4. The Operations Group Commander (4OG/CC) will:

   a. Ensure all flying squadrons comply with this directive and complete required briefs, inspections, and corrective actions prior to resuming flight activity.

   b. Designate an OG Safety POC (name, rank, and contact information) and provide that POC to Wing Safety no later than 0900 local, 15 May 2026.

   c. Coordinate with Maintenance Group leadership to resolve any maintenance or configuration issues that could affect flight safety.

5. Exceptions to this suspension (e.g., launch to save life, limb, or national-level tasking) require written approval from the Wing Commander.

6. Point of contact for this memorandum is Maj Emily R. Carter, Wing Safety Officer, 4FW/SE, DSN 312-555-0102, emily.carter@usaf.mil, or Capt Ryan T. Alvarez, Chief of Flight Safety, 4OG/SE, DSN 312-555-0150.

FOR THE COMMANDER

JOHN A. SMITH, Col, USAF Commander, 4th Fighter Wing

```

```

memo_for:
  - 88 CS/SC
memo_from: []
subject: "Temporary SIPR Tokens for Deploying Maintainers (Suspense: 2026-09-20)"
date: ""
authority_line: ""
signature_block:

letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE

letterhead_seal: dod
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
tag_line: ""
classification:
  value: UNCLASSIFIED
dissemination: ""
references: []
cc: []
distribution: []
attachments: []
memo_style: usaf
font_size: 12
~~~

1. The purpose of this memorandum is to task the Communications Squadron to issue temporary SIPR tokens to 40 deploying maintainers.

2. Action required.

   a. Issue temporary SIPR tokens to the 40 deploying maintainers provided by the 88th Mission Support Group (88 MSG) Personnel Readiness office via secure token request.

   b. Validate each recipient’s deploying status, work role authorization, and need for access to SIPRNet systems prior to token issuance.

   c. Ensure tokens are configured for temporary use only and are set to expire in accordance with the gaining unit’s deployment timeframe as directed by 88 MSG.

   d. Record token serial numbers, issuance dates, recipient names/unique identifiers, and accountable hand-off confirmation.

   e. Provide a signed issuance status roster to 88 MSG Personnel Readiness no later than the suspense date.

3. Suspense. Provide confirmation of token issuance to 88 MSG Personnel Readiness by 2026-09-20.

4. Point of contact. If unable to meet the suspense or if additional guidance is required, coordinate with 88 MSG Personnel Readiness at (XXX) XXX-XXXX.

~~~
$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
memo_for:
  - 88 CS/SC
memo_from:
  - 445 AW/CC
  - 2130 Eighth Street
  - Wright-Patterson AFB OH 45433-7101
subject: "Temporary SIPR Token Support for 40 Deploying Maintainers (Suspense: April 30, 2025)"
date: ""
authority_line: ""
signature_block:
  - FIRST M. LAST, Colonel, USAF
  - Commander
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
  - HEADQUARTERS 445TH AIRLIFT WING
  - WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE, OHIO
letterhead_seal: dow
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
tag_line: ""
classification:
  value: ""
dissemination: ""
references: []
cc:
  - 445 AMW/XP
  - 445 MXG/CC
distribution: []
attachments: []
memo_style: usaf
font_size: 12
~~~

Request your squadron issue temporary SIPRNet tokens and associated user access support for 40 maintainers assigned to the 445th Airlift Wing deployment. Complete issuance no later than April 30, 2025, to support deployment processing and mission preparation.

Coordinate with the 445th Maintenance Group to validate the roster, confirm each member's authorization and training requirements, and schedule token issuance. Provide the supported unit a consolidated appointment schedule and identify any member whose request cannot be completed by the suspense.

Ensure tokens are issued, accounted for, and maintained in accordance with applicable Department of the Air Force cybersecurity, user-access, and communications security procedures. Do not issue a token until all required identity, authorization, and training checks are complete. Brief each recipient on proper safeguarding, reporting, and return or destruction requirements before departure.

Provide completion status to 445 AMW/XP and 445 MXG/CC by close of business April 30, 2025. Include the number issued, the number pending, the reason for each pending request, and the earliest projected completion date. Direct questions or requests for clarification to 445 AMW/XP.

Coordinate with the deploying units and the 445th Airlift Wing information protection and communications points of contact to validate each maintainer's identity, eligibility, account requirement, and deployment need before issuance. This memorandum tasks the 88th Communications Squadron (88 CS/SC) to issue temporary SIPR tokens to support an upcoming deployment of maintenance personnel from the 88th Maintenance Group.

1. Action. 88 CS will issue forty (40) temporary SIPR tokens to identified deploying maintainers to enable classified mission-related communications while deployed.

2. Requirements.

a. 88 CS will coordinate with 88 MXG operations and unit deployment managers to receive a roster of the 40 maintainers requiring tokens. The roster will include full name, rank, DoD ID, unit, and estimated deployment dates.

b. Tokens will be issued as temporary credentials with expiration dates matching the deploying members' authorized deployment periods. Tokens must be configured per applicable DAF and DoD guidance for SIPR access and information assurance.

c. 88 CS will maintain an issuance roster and return/expiration accountability record, and provide a copy to 88 MXG plans (88 MXG/CP) upon completion of issuance.

3. Security and accountability. 88 CS will ensure issuance and handling follow applicable information assurance and physical security procedures. No Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is included with this tasking.

4. Coordination and support. 88 MXG will provide the deployment roster and any required authorization letters or orders no later than 48 hours after receipt of this memorandum.

5. Point of contact. For issuance coordination and questions, contact the 88 MXG deployment office at 88 MXG/CP or the 88 CS Security Office.

6. Suspense. Complete issuance and provide the issuance/ accountability report to 88 MXG/CP by 2026-09-09.

FOR THE COMMANDER

JOHN A. DOE, Col, USAF Commander, 88th Maintenance Group
