This memorandum establishes procedures for responding to requests for patient medical records and other protected health information (PHI) received by the 81st Medical Group. Treat each request as controlled unclassified information (CUI) and limit access, use, and disclosure to personnel with an official need to know.

Before releasing any record, route the request to the 81 MDG/SGH Privacy Officer. The Privacy Officer will verify the requester's identity and authority, determine whether the requested disclosure is permitted or required, and document the disposition. Do not release records directly to a requester, an external provider, an attorney, a family member, or another government organization without Privacy Officer review, even when the requester presents an authorization or states that the request is urgent.

At a minimum, the request package must identify the patient, specify the records and date range sought, state the purpose of the request, identify the intended recipient, and include a valid authorization when one is required. Requests involving minors, deceased patients, personal representatives, subpoenas, litigation, law enforcement, occupational or safety investigations, or disclosures outside the Department of Defense must be referred to the Privacy Officer and 81 FSS/JA before any response is sent.

Use approved systems and transmission methods for all PHI. Do not place PHI in unrestricted email, personal cloud storage, removable media, or informal messaging applications. Verify the recipient and address immediately before transmission, use the required encryption or other approved safeguards, and retain the request, review record, authorization, response, and transmission confirmation in the designated patient-records system.

If an unauthorized disclosure, misdirected transmission, loss, or suspected compromise occurs, stop further distribution and notify the Privacy Officer and the 81 MDG/SGH chain of command immediately. Do not delete, alter, or attempt to retrieve evidence without direction. The Privacy Officer will coordinate reporting, mitigation, and any required notification with legal and information-protection officials.

Questions about this memorandum or a specific request will be directed to the 81 MDG/SGH Privacy Officer at 228-555-0147. The attached checklist may be used to screen and route requests, but it does not replace Privacy Officer or legal review.

1. PURPOSE. This memorandum documents a request for Protected Health Information (PHI) maintained by the 21st Medical Group (21 MDG) and establishes handling instructions for release as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) under applicable Privacy and Records authorities.

2. REQUEST BASIS. The receiving office (21 SPT/SGS) is requesting PHI to support an official, mission-related review consistent with permitted disclosures and the HIPAA Privacy Rule. The request includes the minimum necessary data elements needed to accomplish the stated purpose.

3. RECORDS REQUEST DETAILS. a. Requested record type(s): outpatient encounter summaries, relevant diagnostic test results, and medication lists from 2025-01-01 through 2026-08-31. b. Patient identifier(s): name and DoD ID number as provided in Attachment 1. c. Specific date ranges and locations: visits occurring at JB Elmendorf-Richardson and associated contractor facilities as listed in Attachment 1. d. Format and delivery: electronic transfer via approved DoD channels to the named point of contact (POC) listed in the request.

4. CUI/PRIVACY HANDLING INSTRUCTIONS. a. Marking and distribution: any responsive PHI will be handled as CUI and shared only with authorized individuals performing the stated function. b. Safeguards: access will be limited on a need-to-know basis; systems used for transfer will meet applicable confidentiality and access-control requirements. c. Redaction review: 21 MDG will redact information not necessary to the stated purpose and will withhold data required by law to be protected.

5. RELEASE CONTROLS. a. Accounting of disclosures: a disclosure accounting will be maintained per applicable retention requirements. b. Verification: before release, 21 MDG will verify the requesting office’s authorization and the identity of the POC. c. Timing: PHI will be provided within the timeframes applicable to access/disclosure requests, subject to record retrieval and redaction review.

6. POINTS OF CONTACT. The 21 MDG Privacy and Information Protection office will serve as the primary coordination point for authorization verification, redaction considerations, and secure delivery.

7. ACTION. a. 21 SPT/SGS will confirm that the request includes the minimum necessary information and that the POC is authorized to receive CUI. b. 21 MDG will process the request, apply necessary redactions, and deliver responsive records through approved secure channels.

> If any portion of the request is ambiguous or lacks minimum-necessary justification, 21 MDG will return the request for clarification prior to release.

This memorandum documents the 375th Medical Group's handling of a recent request for Protected Health Information (PHI) received 28 August 2026 and provides instructions for authorized release consistent with controlling authorities.

1. Background. On 28 August 2026, the 375 MDG Privacy Office received a written request from an external legal representative seeking PHI for patient John A. Sample (DOB: 1985-04-12). The request included a signed authorization form dated 27 August 2026 and identification for the requester. The Privacy Office preliminarily validated the identity of the requester and the authenticity of the authorization, but additional verification is required before release.

2. Authorities. Release of PHI is governed by 45 C.F.R. §§160 and 164 (HIPAA Privacy Rule), Department of Defense Medical Records directives, and DoDM 5200.48 concerning Controlled Unclassified Information. When CUI is involved, follow the classification and dissemination controls stated above and consult the unit Privacy Officer.

3. Analysis.

   a. The authorization provided covers treatment records for the period 01 January 2020 through 31 December 2020 and is limited to diagnostic reports and outpatient visit summaries. It does not explicitly authorize release of behavioral health notes, substance abuse treatment records, or third-party psychotherapy notes, which require a separate, specific authorization under applicable law.

   b. The requester represents a non-federal party. Before release to external entities, the Privacy Office must verify the requester’s legal authority (e.g., power of attorney, court order) or receive an authorization that meets HIPAA requirements. Where a court order or subpoena is presented, consult the local SJA and follow DoD release procedures.

4. Action.

# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE / HEADQUARTERS SPACE OPERATIONS COMMAND
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Orbital Conjunction Data Sharing
date: "2026-12-08"
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - KIRA L. DONOVAN, Col, USSF
  - Director of Intelligence
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
  - HEADQUARTERS SPACE OPERATIONS COMMAND
letterhead_seal: dow
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: "CUI"
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: []
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12
---
The space domain community is sharing orbital conjunction data with relevant stakeholders to enhance situational awareness and operational safety. This data sharing initiative is aimed at fostering transparency and collaboration among space operators.

This memorandum emphasizes the importance of maintaining clear communication channels and secure data handling procedures to protect sensitive information while promoting operational efficiency.

The 57th Medical Group is committed to safeguarding patient information and pursuant to 45 CFR Part 160 and 164, we have verified the requester’s authorization to receive the specified PHI.

The requested information will be released only after thorough validation of identity and authorization, ensuring that all procedures comply with the regulatory framework.

Please refer to the attached HIPAA Records Request Form and Medical Records Release Guidelines for detailed instructions and procedural requirements related to this request.

Questions or concerns regarding this memorandum or the handling of PHI requests should be directed to the Chief of the Medical Records Office, Lt Col Karen L. Jenkins, at extension 1234 or email karen.jenkins@usaf.mil.

Thank you for your attention to this sensitive matter.

# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.

subject: Waiver Request—Local Unit Procedures for Aircraft Mission-Ready Inspections
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.

# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD.   - JOHN A. MITCHELL, Lt Col, USAF

    lines:

    text: AFMAN 11-2MDS, Aircraft Mission-Ready Procedures, 2023-10-15

    text: Waiver analysis package and risk assessment, 2026 Jun 05
  - islands: []
    lines:
      - containers: []
        kind: para
    marks: []
    text: Proposed local checklist and implementation plan, 2026 Jun 05
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

Sir:

I request a waiver to apply an updated inspection sequence for aircraft mission-ready readiness checks at the 99th Operations Squadron. The proposed change would allow us to align inspection timing with sortie-generation windows while maintaining compliance with required safety-of-flight parameters.

The waiver is requested for the period 2026-07-01 through 2027-06-30. During this period, 99 OSS will use the attached local checklist and will continue to track inspection outcomes in the 99 OG quality database. We will also conduct weekly supervisor-led reviews to ensure any deviations are identified and corrected immediately.

Supporting rationale and risk mitigation are included in the attached waiver analysis package and implementation plan.

Please indorse accordingly.

//SIGNED//

1. I request a waiver of the 30-day local continuation training requirement for two assigned instructor pilots in the 33d Training Squadron. Due to a combination of mandatory temporary duty, aircraft maintenance backlog, and a three-day mission standdown, the affected aircrew cannot complete the requirement within the prescribed window without disrupting scheduled student sorties.

2. Granting this waiver will allow the squadron to preserve the current training syllabus, avoid unnecessary sortie cancellations, and maintain continuity for the June 2026 class. The requested waiver applies only to the two named instructor pilots in Attachment 1 and expires upon completion of their next scheduled continuation training event.

3. I certify the waiver will not adversely affect mission accomplishment, safety, or readiness, and I request group commander approval and wing concurrence.

memo_style: usaf
font_size: 12
~~~

Request waiver of the requirement in AFI 21-101, paragraph 9.3.4, for a dedicated backshop production superintendent during the period 2026 June 15 through 2026 September 30. The 23d Fighter Squadron is temporarily operating with a vacant position while its authorized superintendent completes a permanent change of station and the replacement reports.

The squadron will remain compliant with all aircraft safety, inspection, and documentation requirements. During the requested period, the assistant operations officer will conduct the daily production review, the lead production supervisor will perform the required technical oversight, and the 366th Maintenance Group will review the squadron's production metrics weekly. The attached justification identifies the affected requirement, operational impact, controls, and termination criteria.

Approval of this waiver will prevent an avoidable reduction in sortie-generation capacity while preserving maintenance discipline and commander visibility. The waiver will terminate automatically on 2026 September 30, or earlier upon assignment and qualification of the replacement superintendent.

~~~
$kind: indorsement
from: 4TH AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE GROUP/CC
for: 23 FS/CC
date: 2026-06-12
authority_line: ""
signature_block:
  - MARCUS T. HOLLOWAY, Col, USAF
  - Commander
format: standard
action: approve
~~~

I have reviewed the request and the attached risk mitigation plan. The proposed controls provide appropriate oversight and preserve aircraft safety and maintenance compliance during the temporary vacancy.

I approve the waiver request and forward it to the 366th Fighter Wing Commander for final action.

~~~
$kind: indorsement
from: 366TH FIGHTER WING/CC
for: 4TH AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE GROUP/CC
date: 2026-06-16
authority_line: ""
signature_block:
  - ELENA R. WHITAKER, Brig Gen, USAF
  - Commander
format: separate_page
action: approve
~~~

I have reviewed the waiver request, the group commander's indorsement, and the risk mitigation measures described in the package. The temporary exception is limited in scope and duration, and the proposed controls are sufficient to manage the associated risk.

I approve the waiver of AFI 21-101, paragraph 9.3.4, for the 23d Fighter Squadron from 2026 June 15 through 2026 September 30, subject to the stated controls and automatic termination criteria.

# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Tactics Review Board # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-02-22 # date<YYYY-MM-DD>
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for the action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - MAJ ELLEN P. SHAW, USAF
  - Chief of Tactics
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - ORG1/SYMBOL
  - ORG2/SYMBOL
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from: []
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: ORM Pulse Survey
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-03-17
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - MAJ THEO J. ALVAREZ, USAF
  - Chief of Safety
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: []
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: []
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
t_ATTACHMENTS: []
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12

# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 18 OG/CC
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
memo_from:
  - 18 OSS/CC
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Airfield Driving Program Audit
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-05-02
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
authority_line: ""
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block:
  - NOAH E. SIMMS, Lt Col, USAF
  - Commander, 18 OSS
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title:
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: ""
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: ""
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification:
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: ""
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*" ]
references: []
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0 # keep verbatim
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - SEE DISTRIBUTION
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from:
  - 355 FW/CC
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: Wing Stand-Up Agenda
# YYYY-MM-DD, printed in the format the Memo Style field selects. Leave blank to use today's date.
date: 2026-06-27
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. - Conduct a targeted follow-up walkthrough of UCC information flow and reporting timelines to ensure consistent status reporting during continuity events.

3. The above action items will be tracked to closure through the appropriate squadron continuity and UCC governance processes.

   a. Update and redistribute the squadron COOP plan to reflect current personnel and contact information.

   c. Assign recurring training and role validation for key COOP positions, to include cross-training of primary and alternate personnel.

4. Capt Jordan Hale will present these action items at the next UCC meeting and track completion through unit action logs.

This memorandum is for the record.

Memorandum for Record

On 2 April 2026, a near-miss occurred on the flightline involving an Aircraft Ground Equipment (AGE) tug during pushback operations near the flightline service area. While the tug and accompanying support personnel were maneuvering in the vicinity of active aircraft, a miscommunication regarding clearance and movement direction created a narrow margin between the tug and an inbound aircraft taxiing path. There were no reported injuries or damage following the incident. Immediate actions included a halt to operations, a stand-down of the affected shift for a safety briefing, and a review of standard operating procedures for tug operations in proximity to active runways.

Witnesses:

> Maj. John A. Smith, USAF Capt. Maria L. Chen, USAF SSgt. Kevin B. Turner, USAF

Further details, corrective actions, and any contributing factors will be documented in the aviation safety follow-up report and reviewed by the Wing Safety Office.

```

1. Purpose. Document a near-miss on the flightline involving an AGE tug on 2 April 2026.

2. Date/Time. 2026-04-02, approximately 1430 local.

3. Location. Flightline ramp area, AGE staging/turnaround lane.

4. Situation. During aircraft ground operations, an AGE tug (operator on foot) maneuvered adjacent to active work areas. While repositioning, the tug came within close proximity of ground personnel/vehicles moving in the same general area.

5. What Happened (Synopsis).

   a. The operator initiated a repositioning turn at low speed while monitoring immediate surroundings.

   b. Ground personnel with mission-tasked movement entered the area of the tug’s projected path.

   c. The operator stopped and secured the tug before contact; the tug did not strike personnel or equipment.

6. Immediate Actions Taken.

   a. Tug was stopped and removed from the immediate working area.

   b. Personnel were directed to re-establish separation and conform to current ground-movement procedures.

   c. The supervisor on duty was notified and an on-the-spot safety brief was conducted.

7. Witnesses (Roster).

> SGT LUCAS MARTINEZ, USAF\
> TSgt NATALIE WRIGHT, USAF\
> AMN RYAN KIM, USAF\
> CIVILIAN JORDAN REED, Contractor

8. Observed Contributing Factors.

   a. Tug route/turn geometry placed ground movement in the same corridor.

   b. Limited situational cues at the intersection point reduced early recognition of converging paths.

9. Corrective/Preventive Actions.

   a. Reinforce AGE tug movement boundaries and required spotter/signal procedures during ground-activity briefs.

   b. Update local signage/marker placement in the maneuver area to improve visibility of pedestrian/vehicle routing.

   c. Review this event during the next safety stand-down and incorporate into ground-operations training.

10. Point of Contact. 1st Fighter Wing Safety Office.

On 2 April 2026 at approximately 0915 local, a ground-based AGE (Aerospace Ground Equipment) tug operating on the 1st Fighter Wing flightline nearly contacted a parked F-35 aircraft at Parking Spot 7. The tug operator, while repositioning palletized support equipment, misjudged clearance and proceeded within an estimated 2 feet of the aircraft's left wing leading edge before stopping. No contact occurred and no damage to the aircraft or equipment was observed.

The incident occurred during routine morning operations with normal visibility and dry ramp conditions. The tug was towing a palletized airstart unit and was being operated at a reduced speed. Preliminary crew interviews indicate the operator's attention was diverted momentarily while confirming tie-downs on the load. Contributing factors under initial review include human factors (brief distraction), close spacing of parked aircraft, and workload during a high-tempo shift change.

Immediate actions taken:

- Operations were halted in the immediate area until a safety brief was conducted for nearby ground crews.

- The tug operator was removed from flightline duties pending supervisory debrief and administrative follow-up.

- Affected personnel provided written statements and the area was inspected for damage; none was found.

- Squadron leadership was notified at 0930 and a hazard report was initiated in accordance with Wing safety procedures.

Preliminary recommendations:

- Reemphasize minimum clearance standards and tow-team communication protocols during the next sortie brief.

- Conduct an immediate refresher for AGE tug operators on distraction mitigation and movement clearance procedures.

- Review aircraft parking plan for Parking Spot 7 to evaluate spacing and traffic flow during peak shift changes.

Witness roster:

> CHEN, AVERY, Maj, USAF\
> SMITH, JAMES, TSgt, USAF\
> RODRIGUEZ, MARIA, SSgt, USAF\
> WILLIAMS, KEVIN, Civ, AGE Technician

This memorandum documents the near-miss for record and initiates the Wing-level safety investigation. A final mishap report will be produced following completion of interviews and any required technical inspections.

# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.

  - 42ABW/A1
  - 42ABW/SF
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: "Implementation of *DAFI 36-2110* Total Force Assignments (Suspense: 30 Jan 2026)"
date: 2026-01-06
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.

$quill: usaf_memo@0.3.0
$kind: main
# U.S. Air Force and Space Force Official Memorandum
# Organization or office symbol, rendered in uppercase. To address a specific person, add their rank and name in parentheses: 'ORG/SYMBOL (LT COL JANE DOE)'. For a long list, enter 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' and name the recipients in the Distribution field.
memo_for:
  - 42ABW/A1
  - 42ABW/SF
# The office symbol alone when every recipient is on this installation. The full mailing address as well when any recipient is elsewhere, so they can write back. Leave blank for a Memorandum for Record, which prints no FROM line.
# e.g. [ORG/SYMBOL, Organization Name, 123 Street Ave, City ST 12345-6789]
memo_from: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Keep it brief. Capitalize the first letter of each word except articles, prepositions, and conjunctions. Put any suspense date in parentheses. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. Subject of the Memorandum
subject: "Implementation of *DAFI 36-2110* Total Force Assignments (Suspense: 30 Jan 2026)"
date: 2026-01-06
# Line telling the reader the signer acted for the commander, the command section, or the headquarters, printed in uppercase above the signature block. AFH 33-337 words it 'FOR THE COMMANDER', or the appropriate title where the head of your organization holds one other than commander. Fill it in when the commander's designated representative signs for a specific action, when the memo carries the commander's position or the coordinated position of the headquarters staff, or when a staff member directs action or announces policy within their own area of responsibility. Leave blank — the usual case — when the commander signs, when the memo gives the opinion of a unit, directorate, division, office, or branch, or when it goes outside the DoD. Leave blank as well when the deputy or vice commander signs while the commander is temporarily away, unless command action is directed by law and requires an indication of delegation.
# e.g. FOR THE COMMANDER
authority_line: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Line 1: Name in UPPERCASE as signed, grade, and service. Line 2: Duty title.
signature_block: !must_fill # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - FIRST M. LAST, Rank, USAF
  - Duty Title
# Letterhead lines, top to bottom, all rendered in uppercase. The first is the department title, set larger than the rest. Change that line only for a Joint Command or a DoW agency. The lines below it are your unit's full organization name.
# e.g. [DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE, "HEADQUARTERS [UNIT NAME]"]
letterhead_title: # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
  - DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE
# Department of War (DoW) or Department of Defense (DoD) seal, shown at the top left of the letterhead. Leave blank for no seal.
letterhead_seal: dow # enum<dow | dod>
# Bold-caps line below the seal. Nothing prints when it is blank, or when there is no seal.
letterhead_seal_subtitle: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Organizational motto, centered in the footer of every page. Supports Markdown emphasis: *italics*, **bold**.
tag_line: "" # richtext(inline)<markdown>
# Classification marking, banner-printed at the top and bottom of every page. Leave blank for no banner, which is what an unclassified document normally carries. Mark per DAFI 16-1404, DoDM 5200.48 for CUI, and applicable DoD guidance.
# when CUI: controlled_by, poc, category, limited_dissemination
classification: # enum<UNCLASSIFIED | CUI | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET>
  value: ""
# Suffix appended to the banner after a double slash, rendered in uppercase: 'NF' prints as CUI//NF. Leave blank for no suffix.
dissemination: "" # plaintext(inline)<plain>
# Cite each reference by organization, type, date, and title. Two or more print as a References block lettered (a), (b), (c); a single one prints in parentheses after the subject, per AFH 33-337. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["AFMAN 33-326, 25 November 2011, *Preparing Official Communications*", "AFI 33-360, *Publications and Forms Management*"]
references: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# Offices or people receiving a courtesy copy, one per line.
# e.g. ["Rank and Name, ORG/SYMBOL"]
cc: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Every recipient, listed here when 'SEE DISTRIBUTION' stands in the Memo For field.
# e.g. [ORG1/SYMBOL, ORG2/SYMBOL]
distribution: [] # array<plaintext(inline)<plain>>
# Attachments in the order the memo mentions them. Describe each briefly; do not write 'as stated' or abbreviate. A lone attachment prints unnumbered, two or more are numbered. Italicize publication titles with *asterisks*.
# e.g. ["Attachment description, YYYY MMM DD"]
attachments: [] # array<richtext(inline)<markdown>>
# USAF memorandum or DAF headquarters memorandum, per AFH 33-337. DAF dates as 'September 15, 2026' rather than '15 September 2026', and leaves top-level paragraphs unnumbered with a first-line indent.
memo_style: usaf # enum<usaf | daf>
# Body text size in points; decimals allowed, such as 11.5. AFH 33-337 §5 specifies 12.
font_size: 12 # number
~~~

The implementation of *DAFI 36-2110* is a significant step toward aligning our force assignment procedures with the latest directives. It is essential that all relevant personnel are acquainted with the new guidelines and adhere strictly to the updated protocols to ensure a seamless transition.

Leadership must emphasize the importance of compliance with this directive, particularly considering the upcoming deadline. Continuous oversight and support from command will facilitate adherence and successful implementation across the entire organization.

> Col RHEA T. GOMEZ, Commander

To: 4 OSS/CC Re: Additional Manning for Night Flying Operations

The 4th Fighter Wing requires five additional SOF-qualified controllers for a 30-day surge to support enhanced night flying operations. OSS is directed to identify and confirm five qualified controllers, with at least 1-2 years of operational night-flying experience and current SOF qualifications, to report prepared for duty by 1 June 2026.

OSS will coordinate surge staffing with the 4 FW/CC staff, ensuring all identified personnel meet SOF qualification standards and are cleared for temporary duty as required. Recommendations should include availability, projected shift coverage, and any anticipated training needs to ensure continuity of operations throughout the surge period, ending 30 June 2026.

Signature: Marcus D. Ellison, Commander
